مُنْجَرِدٌ (assumed tropical:) A horse having short, and little, hair: (EM pp. 39 and 40:) or sharp, or vigorous, in pace, [and] having little hair. (Har p. 455.) ―
-b2- مَا أَنْتَ بِمْنْجَرِدِ السِّلْكِ, (AZ, A, TA,) or ↓ بِمْتَجّرِّدِ السِّلْكِ, (so in a copy of the A,) said to one who is shy, or bashful, [meaning (assumed tropical:) Thou art] not free from shyness in appearing [before others]: (AZ, TA:) or (tropical:) thou art not celebrated, or well-known. (A, TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
